request: Opening the application again should bring its existing window forward instead of showing the shared-data lock error.
implementation: Native, per-Windows-user and interactive-session instance mutex, independent of executable location or release channel.

Before claiming the new mutex, recognize older main windows by exact window class/title, executable basename, ProductName, Windows user SID and session. Prefer the original process if multiple older windows exist. No profile contents are opened for detection.

Older copies do not receive an unsupported activation message. Use a bounded Windows restore/foreground request instead. This also works while a preceding candidate has opened its own lock-error window.

A secondary launch waits briefly for startup, sends a bounded activation request to the marked owner window, and exits before Documents resolution, Flutter bootstrap, saved-data loading, or Fish startup.
Restore minimized owners; preserve maximization and native modal dialogs. Respect Windows focus policy, with taskbar flashing if foreground activation is denied.
Normal exit or a process crash releases the OS mutex. There is no persistent single-instance state file.
Shared-profile writer lease, format verification, location/migration logic, close/save barrier, and maintenance protections remain independent and unchanged.
Velopack lifecycle hooks run before UI routing; independent --reference Minigame Helper launches do not acquire or publish the primary instance.
boundaries: Older already-built versions lack the new handshake but can now be brought forward without changing their binaries. Returning to an older running copy does not upgrade it; close it to switch to a newer version.
The native UI mutex is session-local; the existing file lease still prevents competing writers across Windows sessions. No attempt is made to activate another session's desktop.

An unresponsive/unready owner exceeding the bounded wait gets a short opening/closing notice, not a competing application startup. Real profile incompatibility and other startup failures remain visible.
No saved data, installed version, shortcuts, reference/calculation code, or public release changed.

verification.native: 42 checks using this exact coordinator in synthetic processes on a private, never-activated Windows desktop. Includes an older executable with matching metadata/window identity, no new launch protocol, and a held synthetic file lease; startup races, rapid secondaries, another executable path, minimize/maximize/modal behavior, helper exclusion, timeout, exit and abandoned-mutex recovery.
verification.baselineReproduction: The same regression harness, linked to the unchanged preceding coordinator, reproduced five legacy-activation failures (40 checks). The corrected coordinator passed all 42 checks (two additional discovery assertions).
verification.readOnlyLiveDetection: The exact new native discovery function identified PID 38052, the previously verified real shared-lock owner. It did not activate, close, launch or modify the real application or read saved data.
verification.regression: 43 persistence, real multiprocess writer-lease, startup surface and close-handshake checks.
verification.fullApplicationLaunch: Not performed against personal data. User testing remains separate; APPDATA-only redirection is not a valid full-app isolation harness.
